A1.justification: Both complete 23-page PDFs describe the same FlashRNN work. Text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–K are readable and can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPU runtime benchmarks, SlimPajama language-model training results and parity extrapolation experiments in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including the runtime figures, language-model results in Tables 1 and 3, and parity accuracies in Table 2.

M1.justification: The recurrent architectures, gradient procedures, head-wise parallelization, CUDA/Triton kernels and ConstrINT optimization remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendices A–E.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GPU runtime scenarios, SlimPajama language-modeling task and synthetic parity extrapolation task. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: vanilla PyTorch, cuDNN-backed nn.LSTM, Haste and FlashAttention2 for runtime comparisons, and unchanged language-modeling and parity comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendices J–K retain identical hardware settings, precisions, model configurations, training budgets, metrics and testing procedures. The new computing-resource acknowledgments do not report revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: Appendices G–H retain the same roofline analysis, kernel-size limits, runtime sensitivity experiments, gate-preactivation comparison and numerical-error analysis. No supplementary analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Both versions report runtime averages over 1,000 measurement iterations and parity results averaged over three seeds. Seed information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All runtime plots, language-model training times and perplexities in Tables 1 and 3, and parity accuracies in Table 2 are unchanged. The appendices contain no added, removed or corrected results.

T1.justification: The RNN and backpropagation equations, architectural definitions, constraint-solving formulation and computational-complexity analysis are unchanged, including their appendix material.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about state tracking, head-wise parallelization, ConstrINT, speedups and supported hidden sizes.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are retained, including hardware-memory constraints, unexplained convergence differences from cuDNN, training-time spikes and possible future hardware optimizations.

D1.justification: The Reproducibility Statement replaces a promised GitHub release including training scripts with a present-tense code-availability statement and repository link. The same link already appears in v1's abstract, so this clarifies disclosure without establishing a new release or changed repository contents.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and the related-work discussion preserves the same research positioning. Its paragraph reflow does not change citations or substantive comparisons.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgments section, merges two related-work paragraphs and revises the code-availability sentence. The scientific narrative and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgments shift the ethics and reproducibility statements downward and move the bibliography's start from page 10 to page 11. Local spacing and pagination change, while figure and table designs, captions and contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the inconsistent future-release wording by aligning the Reproducibility Statement with availability already stated in the abstract, and adds contributor, computing-resource and funding acknowledgments. These modestly improve clarity and transparency; the scientific evidence, technical documentation and appendices otherwise remain unchanged.
